pages.sovereignty.title: Sovereignty Architecture
pages.sovereignty.s1.title: Local execution — the generator never phones home
pages.sovereignty.s1.p1: Static QR generation — matrix computation, styling, rasterisation and SVG serialisation — runs entirely inside your browser's sandbox, on your own CPU. URLs, vCards, Wi-Fi keys and IBAN strings are never transmitted, never logged and never stored server-side. There is no payload for us to disclose, subpoena or lose.
pages.sovereignty.s1.p2: Consequence: a static code keeps working forever, even if this service disappears. Nothing about it depends on our uptime.
pages.sovereignty.s2.title: EEA infrastructure & transport-layer minimisation
pages.sovereignty.s2.residency: <s>Residency:</s> application servers, managed PostgreSQL, database backups and routing proxies operate strictly inside the European Economic Area.
pages.sovereignty.s2.dynamic: <s>Dynamic resolution:</s> short links and profile hubs (<m>rout.id</m> / <m>rout.be</m>) necessarily traverse network nodes. Standard transport-layer metadata (IP, User-Agent) is processed in memory for real-time routing and immediate DDoS mitigation only.
pages.sovereignty.s2.retention: <s>No long-term retention:</s> full IP addresses are not written to durable storage. Scan analytics are coarse and anonymous — timestamp, country, device family — and are destroyed with the link.
pages.sovereignty.s2.profiling: <s>No profiling:</s> no advertising cookies, no cross-site identifiers, no browser fingerprinting.
pages.sovereignty.s3.title: Sovereign identity — passkeys and your own IdP
pages.sovereignty.s3.passkeys: <s>WebAuthn passkeys:</s> biometric or hardware-key sign-in where the private key never leaves your device, and no shared secret exists to breach.
pages.sovereignty.s3.oidc: <s>Custom OIDC:</s> bring your own identity provider — Keycloak, Authentik or Authelia — so account authority stays with you rather than a platform.
pages.sovereignty.s3.payments: <s>Payment decoupling:</s> regulated fiat rails (SEPA, PayPal, Venmo) are handled by PCI-DSS compliant processors and stay separated from your sovereign identity records.
pages.sovereignty.s4.title: Open source & auditability — AGPLv3 (network copyleft)
pages.sovereignty.s4.body: ROUT is licensed under the <s>GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or later (AGPL-3.0-or-later)</s>. Every claim on this page is checkable against the source: the client-side generator, the redirect handler and the analytics pipeline are all public. The AGPL's network clause means any hosted fork must publish its modifications, so the guarantees travel with the code. Self-hosting is a first-class path, not an afterthought.
